topics.topic: External model-provider trust boundary and permitted disclosure of Registry contact data
questions: Which external model provider receives Registry data, and what trust boundary applies when customer contact data is sent to it?
Does “readable by staff only” describe only Registry API authorization, or does it prohibit the non-staff model provider from processing contact data?
Which external model-provider boundary is accepted, what Registry data may cross it, and does the acceptance include provider retention, logging and subprocessors?
Is the operator's model provider an expressly permitted recipient of customer contact data despite the staff-only rule, and which operator reads or writes may disclose which fields to it?

quotes:
An
  agent works with the owner's own access to Registry's host and could read
  the store itself, so the credential does not keep contact data from it:
  whatever it records or reads passes through its model provider, and the
  owner accepts this (owner, 2026-10-27).

- **Personal data** — the customer's contact data (R0-06); readable by staff
  only (R0-09).

The operator
preparing the owner's WhatsApp link reads the phone from here, as staff. Name, phone, e-mail and language are
all the customer's contact data: personal data, readable by staff only (R0-09),
and erasable as a whole.

Every write needs one of them; recording, correcting, reading or
erasing a customer needs the staff credential.
judgement.divergence: One implementation permits the operator to send all customer contact fields to any configured model provider, including under that provider's retention, logging and subprocessor practices; another permits only the phone needed for the stated message or requires a specifically approved provider with restricted processing. The owner, operator, customer and model provider notice the different disclosure boundary.
judgement.why: The text accepts an external model-provider disclosure while leaving the provider and the permitted extent of that disclosure unnamed, so the trust boundary and observable privacy behavior remain open.

topics.topic: Restart behavior and startup validation for missing, invalid, or inconsistent configuration
questions: What must Registry observably do when required configuration is missing, malformed, internally inconsistent or unreadable at restart?
What does Registry do at restart when credentials, frontend origin or artifact vocabulary configuration is absent, malformed, duplicated or internally inconsistent?
Which configuration entries are mandatory, may the vocabulary or service-token set be empty, and must Registry refuse to start when non-vocabulary configuration is missing or invalid?

judgement.why: P1 already judged the same startup configuration-validation and failure-behavior question on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Required configuration validation and behavior when configuration cannot be applied at startup
quotes:
The owner, as the host's
administrator, changes it outside Registry; a change takes effect when the
instance restarts, and a replaced token stops working at that restart, with no
overlap.
precedent.why: Acceptance and rejection rules for missing, malformed, ambiguous, or unusable configuration, together with their required tests, belong to State 2.

topics.topic: Whether operators may directly access or write the Registry store
questions: Is direct store access by the operator an authorized operating path, merely an acknowledged capability that must not be used, or limited to emergency inspection; and may it ever write the store?

Is direct store access an authorized operator action, merely an acknowledged ability outside the product contract, or something storage permissions must prevent; and is direct writing always forbidden?

quotes:
An
  agent works with the owner's own access to Registry's host and could read
  the store itself, so the credential does not keep contact data from it:
  whatever it records or reads passes through its model provider, and the
  owner accepts this (owner, 2026-10-27).

The Registry frontend and the operator script `onboard_object`. This case
  designs the HTTP service; both are clients of its API, like any consumer, and
  are designed elsewhere; they follow R0-13.
judgement.why: Whether host access may be used for direct store inspection or mutation, and which storage permissions enforce that policy, is an operational-access question for State 4 rather than a missing Registry product action.

topics.topic: Authority granted to trusted host processes
questions: What is a host process trusted to do, given that writes and contact-data reads still require scoped credentials?

topics.topic: Customer data permitted in unauthenticated project context
questions: Does the unauthenticated context contain only `customer_ref` and erasure state, or any Customer name, phone, e-mail or language?

topics.topic: Cutover and overlap behavior when replacing the staff credential
questions: When the staff credential is replaced, does the old credential stop working at the same restart with no overlap, or is a different rotation rule intended?

topics.topic: Deployment check proving Registry is unreachable beyond the host
questions: What concrete deployment check establishes that no Registry port is reachable beyond the host, what observable result constitutes success, and what happens when the check fails?

topics.topic: Host administrative-access authentication, delegation, and secret handling
questions: What authenticates administrative access to the host, who may hold or delegate it, and is that credential covered by the stated vault and non-disclosure rules?

topics.topic: Required format, entropy, and generation of credentials and service tokens
questions: What formats, minimum entropy and generation mechanism make a staff credential or service token acceptable to Registry?

topics.topic: Whether owner-host agents may access Registry secret configuration
questions: Can an agent acting through the owner's host access read Registry's secret-bearing configuration, or is that access technically separated from the owner's configuration access?
